title: Kamphaeng Phet Nature & Waterfalls 2026 — Khlong Lan, Mae Wong | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Kamphaeng Phet's nature side in Thailand: 100m Khlong Lan Waterfall, Mae Wong's Chong Yen sea of mist, and Phra Ruang hot springs — with fees, hours and the best times to go.
keywords: Kamphaeng Phet nature, Khlong Lan Waterfall, Mae Wong National Park, Chong Yen, Phra Ruang hot springs
intro: Most people know Kamphaeng Phet for its historical park, but the other half of the province is the western forest that runs all the way to the border. There's Khlong Lan Waterfall dropping a hundred-odd metres, Mae Wong National Park where you can climb up to a sea of mist in the middle of the hot season, and a hot spring where you can soak your feet for free. This is the nature-side guide to Kamphaeng Phet — where to go, when it looks its best, and what you'll pay.

blocks.html: Kamphaeng Phet sits between the Ping River lowlands and the western mountains that wall it off toward Tak. The west side of the province is full of forest and hills, with two big national parks — Khlong Lan and Mae Wong — plus a hot spring close to town. You can drive to all of them in a day from the city centre, so it's a good escape if you want to swap the old town for cold water and green forest.

blocks.text: Khlong Lan Waterfall — the big one that's easiest to reach

blocks.html: If you only have time for one spot, make it Khlong Lan Waterfall. It's a single-drop fall pouring off a cliff around 100 metres high and roughly 40 metres wide, fed by the Khun Khlong Lan range that rises over 1,400 metres. At the base there's a large pool you can swim in. What I like is that the walk from the park office to the falls is only about 500 metres on an easy concrete path — doable for older visitors or families with kids, no climbing required.

Khlong Lan has water year-round, but the fullest, greenest stretch is from mid rainy season into the early cool season, roughly September to November. In the dry season the flow drops but it still runs, and the water is clearer. If you're going for a swim, check the flash-flood warning signs before you get in — in the rainy season the water comes down hard and it's freezing cold.

blocks.title: Fees and hours
blocks.html: Khlong Lan National Park is open 08:30–16:30. Entry is 40 THB for Thai adults, 20 THB for Thai children, 200 THB for foreign adults and 100 THB for foreign children, plus 30 THB per car and 20 THB per motorbike. There's a campground at 30 THB per person per night, and park bungalows start around 600 THB. Book ahead in the cool season — it gets busy.

blocks.text: Other waterfalls in the Khlong Lan area

blocks.html: Khlong Lan park covers hundreds of square kilometres, so there's more than just the one waterfall. If you want to go deeper and don't mind the distance, there are more falls and rapids to stop at, each with its own feel.

items.name: Khlong Nam Lai Waterfall
items.blurb: A medium-sized fall that steps down through 9 tiers, each with a shallow pool to soak in. Quieter than Khlong Lan and about 25 km from the park office — good for a short forest walk.

items.name: Rapids & forest campgrounds
items.blurb: The park has several campgrounds, like the Khlong Nam Lai site and ones deeper in the forest, for anyone who wants to stay the night and wake to running water and birdsong.

blocks.text: Mae Wong National Park — up the mountain for the sea of mist

blocks.html: Mae Wong is a large stretch of forest straddling Kamphaeng Phet (Pang Sila Thong district) and Nakhon Sawan. The spot people come for is Chong Yen, the highest point on the Khlong Lan–Umphang road at around 1,340 metres. It's a sunset and sea-of-mist viewpoint with a cool breeze almost all year, averaging under 20°C and dropping to 15°C in the cool season — even when it's over 40°C down below.

Another spot photographers love is Khun Nam Yen, a campground about 24 km from the office where you can take in evergreen hill forest in nearly every direction and catch both sunrise and sunset. If you like camping deep in the forest in cool air, this is where people from Kamphaeng Phet and the surrounding provinces drive up to spend the night in the cool season.

items: Best time — November to February, cool air and the best odds of catching the sea of mist
Getting there — the road up to Chong Yen is a winding mountain route; use a vehicle in good shape and go in daylight
Where to stay — mostly camping, so bring warm gear because the nights get genuinely cold
Come prepared — phone signal is limited, so fill up on fuel and buy food before heading up the mountain

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Chong Yen is far out and it's a long mountain drive — not a quick drive-by stop. If you're set on Mae Wong, set aside the whole day or stay the night; don't expect to drive up for photos and back down within an hour. And check the park's page beforehand to see whether Chong Yen is open at the time, because the route closes in some seasons.

blocks.text: Phra Ruang Hot Springs — a foot soak close to town

blocks.html: If you don't feel like driving far, Phra Ruang Hot Springs is about 22 km from the city centre. It's a natural hot spring bubbling up from 5 sources at around 40–65°C, with the grounds landscaped for an easy stroll. There's an open-air foot-soak pool where you sit on bamboo platforms under a roof for shade — that part is free, and it's a good stop in the late afternoon before heading back into town.

items: Free foot soak — the open-air pool on bamboo platforms, with the water at just the right warmth
Mineral baths — the shared bathhouse is around 30 THB and a private room rents for around 50 THB
Bungalows and a campground — for anyone who wants to stay and unwind, natural-spa style

blocks.html: Kamphaeng Phet's nature spots are spread across the west of the province, so driving yourself is by far the easiest. Here's a two-day, one-night plan I'd lay out — unhurried, with both the waterfall and the mountain.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Khlong Lan Waterfall + a night in the forest

items.activity: Leave Kamphaeng Phet city and drive to Khlong Lan district
items.note: About 1.5 hours; fill up on fuel before you go

items.activity: Reach Khlong Lan park, walk to the waterfall, swim in the pool
Lunch at the park canteen or a spot in Khlong Lan town
Stop at Khlong Nam Lai Waterfall at an easy pace, or take a short nature walk
Pitch a tent or check into a park bungalow and listen to the forest in the evening
items.note: Book bungalows ahead in the cool season

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Up to Mae Wong + a foot soak before heading home

items.activity: Set off for Mae Wong National Park on the Pang Sila Thong side
items.note: Go early for better odds of heavy mist

items.activity: Head up to Chong Yen for the forest views and sea of mist, breathe the cool air
Come down the mountain and grab lunch along the way
Stop at Phra Ruang Hot Springs for a relaxing foot soak before town

blocks.text: What to sort out before a nature trip

items: A car makes it far easier — public transport into the parks is limited, so if you don't have a car, look at renting one or hiring a car from town
Check opening hours — the parks close at 16:30, so don't arrive late; leave time to walk and swim
Watch for floods in the rainy season — always check the warning signs before getting into a waterfall
It really is cold up the mountain in the cool season — Chong Yen and Khun Nam Yen can drop to 15°C, so pack warm clothes
Pack out your trash — many of these spots are protected forest, so bring a bag for your rubbish

faq.q: When is Khlong Lan Waterfall at its best?
faq.a: Khlong Lan has water year-round, but the fullest flow and greenest forest come from mid rainy season into the early cool season, roughly September to November. In the dry season the flow is lighter, but the water is clearer and more comfortable for swimming.

faq.q: How much is entry to Khlong Lan National Park?
faq.a: Thai adults 40 THB, Thai children 20 THB, foreign adults 200 THB, foreign children 100 THB, plus 30 THB per car and 20 THB per motorbike. Open 08:30–16:30.

faq.q: Where is Chong Yen and how do you get there?
faq.a: Chong Yen is in Mae Wong National Park on the Pang Sila Thong side. It's the highest point on the Khlong Lan–Umphang road at around 1,340 metres. The way up is a winding mountain road, so use a vehicle in good shape and go during daylight. Visit in the cool season for a chance at the sea of mist.

faq.q: Is the foot soak at Phra Ruang Hot Springs free?
faq.a: There's an open-air foot-soak pool on bamboo platforms that's free to use. If you want a mineral bath, there's a shared bathhouse for around 30 THB and a private room for around 50 THB. It's about 22 km from the city centre.

faq.q: Do you need your own car to see Kamphaeng Phet's nature spots?
faq.a: It's much easier with a car, since both Khlong Lan and Mae Wong are on the west side of the province and public transport there is limited. If you don't have a car, look at renting one or hiring a car from town.
